opening: Our API is built on Echo (the current main branch), and the way we proxy WebSocket connections, request binding and error responses give our clients confusing results. The binding examples below go through c.Bind with the default binder and JSON serializer.

requirements.m01: We run the proxy middleware in front of a WebSocket service, with other proxies in front of ours. For a WebSocket upgrade request the service only receives a correct X-Forwarded-For when the incoming request carries none: when upstream proxies have already added entries, our proxy passes the header on as it came and its own peer address is missing from the chain, so the service's "rightmost untrusted address" rule picks the wrong client. Plain HTTP requests through the same proxy get the right chain. For WebSocket requests the proxy must append the address it sees the request coming from (the request's real IP, as c.RealIP() reports it) to whatever came in, as a comma-separated list: with no incoming header the service must receive just that address; an incoming header holding one entry A must arrive as "A, <address>"; an incoming comma-separated chain "A, B" must arrive as "A, B, <address>"; and two separate incoming X-Forwarded-For header lines, A and B, must be joined the same way, "A, B, <address>".
requirements.m02: When a query, form or path value cannot be converted to the target field's type, the bind error does not say which field failed: binding number=10a into an int field gives only the bare conversion error (strconv.ParseInt: parsing "10a": invalid syntax). The error should be prefixed with the input field name and a colon, as in "number: strconv.ParseInt: parsing \"10a\": invalid syntax" (inside the HTTP error: code=400, message=Bad Request, err=number: ...), on the first bind of a type and on every later bind of the same type, for slices and for values bound through UnmarshalParam too (for example err=t: 'xxxx' is not an integer). errors.Is and errors.As must still find the original error.
requirements.m03: JSON request bodies are decoded leniently: a body with extra data after the JSON value (another value, or garbage) is accepted and the rest is silently ignored, and a truncated body such as { is reported as "unexpected EOF". A body must contain exactly one JSON value: trailing data is a 400 Bad Request, and a truncated body is reported as code=400, message=Bad Request, err=unexpected end of JSON input.
requirements.m04: We keep reusable problem-details errors as package-level values and return them from handlers, with the RFC 9457 problem-details error handler installed (errors not exposed): for example a value with status 404 and detail "no such widget". Serving it fills the missing fields in on that shared value itself: its type becomes about:blank, its title becomes the status text, and a value with no status gets 500 written into it, so after the first request the value is permanently altered for the whole process and concurrent requests race on it. The response itself is right and must stay so: a GET on such a route answers 404 with the application/problem+json content type and the body {"type":"about:blank","title":"Not Found","status":404,"detail":"no such widget"} followed by a newline. But after the request the shared value must be exactly as it was before: the same status, type, title and detail.
